notes:
Rotolight Anova Pro 2 is a continuous LED + High-Speed-Sync flash studio/location light (not a standard AV signal-chain device), so category/type were forced into the closest generic buckets ("other"/"Other") — none of the provided enums represent lighting fixtures. It appears discontinued/superseded by the Anova Pro 3 (rotolight.com/products/anova-pro-2 now 404s; B&H lists it "No Longer Available"), so this is a historical spec record.

Variants exist: beam angle Standard 50° vs Wide/Ultrawide 110°; color as Bi-Colour (3150-6300K, CRI 96/TLCI 97) or Fixed 5600K (CRI 94/TLCI 91). Ports/I-O are identical across variants. Power draw is 72W at 100% output. Body weighs ~2.6kg (without yoke/barn doors).

Two additional physical items on the rear panel were deliberately left out of the ports list because they don't correspond to a standard AV cable connector in the allowed id set: (1) a "Firmware programming socket" explicitly marked "not intended for use by users" (service-only, manufacturer/distributor use), and (2) a V-Lock battery plate (mounts standard 14.4V V-Lock or Anton Bauer Goldmount-via-adapter batteries as an alternative to the DC-in AC adapter).

Primary source used: the official Rotolight Anova Pro 2 User Manual (v5.49 PDF), mirrored by AV reseller streamingvalley.nl since the manufacturer's own product page for this discontinued model no longer resolves; content and layout match the manual also hosted (paginated) on manualslib.com/manual/1593293/Rotolight-Anova-Pro-2.html. Cross-checked against the B&H Photo Video retailer listing (bhphotovideo.com, "No Longer Available") and the Newsshooter hands-on review (newsshooter.com/2019/01/04/rotolight-anova-pro-2-led-review/), both of which corroborate the 5-pin DMX/RJ45, V-Lock plate, and AC/DC power description. All sources fetched over normal verified HTTPS.

ports.name: DMX In/Out (XLR)
ports.note: 5-pin XLR DMX512 in/out socket, used for daisy-chaining in structured studio cabling.

ports.name: DMX In/Out (RJ45)
ports.note: Carries DMX512 signal over RJ45 (not Ethernet/Art-Net); manual gives no data-rate grade.

ports.name: USB
ports.note: Manual only says 'USB port', reserved for future firmware updates; exact USB connector size/type (e.g. Micro-USB) is not stated and is inferred as the closest common port for this class/era of device.

ports.name: Flash Sync / Trigger Input
ports.note: Manual specifies a 3.5mm MONO jack (TS, not TRS) for third-party PC-sync/flash trigger input; trs-3.5 is the closest id in the allowed connector list.

ports.name: DC In
ports.note: 2.1mm DC barrel socket, 13-17V DC (nominal 15V); powered by supplied 15V/90W AC-DC adapter, or usable with a 14.4V D-Tap source through the same socket.
